title: Using Sentinel-1 and GRACE satellite data to monitor the hydrological variations within the Tulare Basin, California
datasets: JPL ARIA Sentinel-1 InSAR line-of-sight displacement time series

dataset_roles.dataset: JPL ARIA Sentinel-1 InSAR line-of-sight displacement time series

idea.research_question: How do short-term Tulare Basin surface-displacement variations in the JPL ARIA Sentinel-1 InSAR time series co-vary with CSR RL06 Mascon terrestrial-water-storage anomalies?
idea.hypothesis: After separating long-term aquifer compaction from the ARIA LOS displacement series, short-term deformation variations have coherent associations with basin-scale CSR RL06 Mascon storage anomalies.
idea.mechanism: Reference and detrend ARIA LOS displacement, aggregate it to hydrologically comparable intervals, aggregate CSR RL06 Mascon anomalies over Tulare Basin, then test temporal co-variation while preserving their distinct spatial resolutions.
idea.analytical_approach: Joint InSAR–gravimetry time-series analysis with compaction removal, basin aggregation, lag testing and robustness checks
idea.expected_contribution: A reproducible benchmark that preserves the product-specific ARIA InSAR and CSR RL06 Mascon observation contract.
idea.falsification_condition: Reject an idea if it replaces ARIA displacement with Sentinel-1 GRD, replaces CSR RL06 Mascons with deprecated GEE GRACE grids, omits either required product, or cannot demonstrate aligned temporal use.

anchor_context.asset_definition_note: Required inputs are JPL ARIA processed Sentinel-1 InSAR displacement and CSR GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06 Mascon solutions; generic Sentinel-1 GRD and deprecated GEE GRACE grids are not substitutes.
